Definition: a primary word; "else," i.e. different (in many applications):--more, one (another), (an-, some an-)other(-s, -wise).
BiblicalUsage: Another, other, else — and it is everywhere in the Gospels, one hundred and thirty-six times. And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd. And some fell upon stony places, where they had not much earth: and forthwith they sprung up, because they had no deepness of earth; the word is the otherness of the flock and the otherness of the soil.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for other carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the promise in it, that there are other sheep beyond the fold I can see, and the Shepherd is bringing them too.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
